proposed_widenings.name: ClassFeatureEffect.ongoing_state
proposed_widenings.justification: Rage's effect is a persistent state with multiple simultaneous sub-effects, a max duration (10 min), early-termination conditions, and a turn-by-turn renewal mechanic. None of the existing ClassFeatureEffect variants (grant_extra_action, heal_hp) model this. This is the root atom_widening — the tracer throws 'unhandled class-feature effect' on the 'ongoing_state' kind.
proposed_widenings.evidence: While active, your Rage follows the rules below. [...] The Rage lasts until the end of your next turn, and it ends early if you don Heavy armor or have the Incapacitated condition.

proposed_widenings.name: damage_resistance
proposed_widenings.justification: Rage grants resistance to three damage types (BPS) while active. No damage_resistance atom exists anywhere in ClassFeatureEffect. The closest analog in spells is Stoneskin's mechanics, but class features have no resistance effect type.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Damage Resistance. You have Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

proposed_widenings.name: bonus_damage
proposed_widenings.justification: Rage adds a flat bonus (+2/+3/+4 by class level) to damage rolls for Strength weapon attacks and Unarmed Strikes. No bonus_damage class-feature effect atom exists. This is a damage rider conditioned on the attack using Strength, scaling by class level via threshold_tiers.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Rage Damage. When you make an attack using Strength — with either a weapon or an Unarmed Strike — and deal damage to the target, you gain a bonus to the damage that increases as you gain levels as a Barbarian.

proposed_widenings.name: advantage_on_ability
proposed_widenings.justification: Rage grants Advantage on Strength ability checks AND Strength saving throws. No advantage_on_ability class-feature effect atom exists. The mastery surface has modify_roll_advantage but that is a on-hit rider, not an ongoing state effect on the activating creature.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Strength Advantage. You have Advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws.

proposed_widenings.name: disable_actions
proposed_widenings.justification: Rage prohibits maintaining Concentration and casting spells. No disable_actions atom exists. This is a constraint on the Raging creature's available action types while the state is active.
proposed_widenings.evidence: No Concentration or Spells. You can't maintain Concentration, and you can't cast spells.

proposed_widenings.name: early_termination_condition
proposed_widenings.justification: Rage ends early on two conditions: donning Heavy armor or gaining the Incapacitated condition. These are state-watch predicates on the activating creature. No early_termination_condition atom or lifecycle variant handles this pattern.
proposed_widenings.evidence: it ends early if you don Heavy armor or have the Incapacitated condition

proposed_widenings.name: turn_renewal
proposed_widenings.justification: Rage's duration lasts until end of next turn but can be extended each turn by one of: making an attack roll against an enemy, forcing an enemy to make a saving throw, or taking a Bonus Action. This renewal-on-action pattern is entirely absent from the current duration/lifecycle vocabulary (only instantaneous, concentration, timed persist/expire exist).
proposed_widenings.evidence: If your Rage is still active on your next turn, you can extend the Rage for another round by doing one of the following: Make an attack roll against an enemy. Force an enemy to make a saving throw. Take a Bonus Action to extend your Rage.

proposed_widenings.name: UseCountCap.unlimited
proposed_widenings.justification: Level 17+ Barbarian has unlimited Rage uses per day. UseCountCap = { kind: 'fixed' } | ThresholdTiers<number> — neither can express 'unlimited'. A new { kind: 'unlimited' } variant is needed.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Level 17 row of the Barbarian Features table shows 'Unlimited' in the Rages column.

notes: Typecheck passed (JSON is not statically typed). Tracer threw 'unhandled class-feature effect: [object Object]' at traceClassFeatureEffect (tracer.ts:1371) because ClassFeatureEffect = GrantExtraActionEffect | HealHpEffect does not include 'ongoing_state'. The atoms emitted before the throw (class_feature_root, activate, bonus_action_quota, use_count, scale_numeric_bonus, rest_window) confirm the resource/reset mechanics fit the existing surface. The effect subtree is entirely missing. The structural issue is deeper: the activation family was designed for instant one-shot effects; Rage requires a new class_feature_ongoing_effect family with duration, multi-effect payloads, early-termination conditions, and a turn-renewable lifecycle.
